3. The plaintiffs case, in short, was that the suit land belonged to Md. Atir Ullah, Abdul Khaleque, Ramiz Ullah and Akloma Bibi. That Ramiz Ullah was not related to Akloma Bibi and others. That Ramiz Ullah purchased 0.06 acre of land of plot No. 3424 and 0.22 acre, of land of plot No. 3425 from Akloma Bibi. Accordingly, his name was recorded, in D.P Khatian No. 11 corresponding to S.A. Khatian No. 70. That Md. Atir Ullah got 1/5 share measuring 28 decimals out of 1.41 acres of suit land. That subsequently Akloma Bibi died, leaving behind two daughters, defendant Nos. 13-14 who became the owner of 18 decimals of land holding 2/3 sharp and Md. Atir Ullah became the owner of 5 decimals as residuary. That Abdul Khaleq and Abdul Malek, the sons of Majlish Ullah became the owner of 0.025 acre of land each as the residuary. That Atir Ullah died leaving behind 2 sons, Md. Askar and Md. Kanu Mia and one daughter. That Md. Askar became the owner of 0.1320 acre of land out of 33 decimals of land left by Atir Ullah. Md. Askar while owning and enjoying possession of 0.1320 acre of land died leaving behind 4 sons, the plaintiff Nos.1 and 2 and the defendant Nos. 4 and 5, a daughter the plaintiff No. 3 and a wife, the plaintiff No. 4 as his successive heirs. Thus the plaintiff Nos. 1-4 became the owner of 0.085 acre of land who on paying rent to the government were enjoying the possession thereof. That on 19.11.2009 the plaintiffs demanded partition of the suit property upon claiming saham of 0.0805 acre of land. The defendants refused, hence the suit. 

 4. The defendant Nos.1 and.24 contested the suit by filing, separate sets of written statements. The material case of defendant No. 1 is that Aslam Ullah, the father of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and the husband of defendant No. 3 purchased .14 decimals of land from the recorded tenant. Akloma Bibi and others in the year 1959. That the defendant No. 3 also, by the kabala dated 24.01.1961, purchased 15, decimals of land from Akloma Bibi which was duly .recorded in D.P. Khatian. That 0.21 decimal of land of suit plot. No. 2131 belonged to Akloma Bibi and others and that Aslam Ullah vide registered kabala dated 04.05.1979 purchased 0.05 acre of land of plot No. 3465 from Akloma Bibi. That Aslam Ullah vide registered deed dated 25.02.1990 purchased 0.02 acre of land from plot No. 3465 of khatian No. 336. That at the death of Aslam Ullah defendant No. 1 inherited 11 decimals of land of plot No. 3465. 

 11. Mr. N. K. Saha the learned Counsel for the plaintiff-respondents has made submissions supporting the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. The learned Counsel has argued that in this case for partition none of the contesting parties raised any objection as to the correctness of the S.A. khatian of the suit property and in the circumstances there was no necessity at all to send back the case on remand for retrial; that there was no error in the judgment and decree of the trial court and in the circumstances the High Court Division rightly restored the judgment and decree of the trial court by setting aside the judgment and decree of the lower appellate court.
